Time to earn your lunch!
To initiate combat, the first thing Rex needs
to do is [System:Color name=tutorial ]draw his weapon[/System:Color].

To draw your weapon, simply press [System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=A ]
[/System:Color]while [System:Color name=tutorial ]targeting an enemy[/System:Color]. To display the target,
just press [System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=R ][/System:Color].

The [System:Color name=tutorial ]target[/System:Color] is the pink marker
displayed above an enemy's head.

Incidentally, you can also [System:Color name=tutorial ]sheathe your weapon [/System:Color]if
you'd rather not continue a fight. It's as
simple as holding down [System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=R ] [/System:Color]and pressing [System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=B ][/System:Color].

If you approach the [System:Color name=tutorial ]targeted enemy[/System:Color]
with your [System:Color name=tutorial ]weapon drawn[/System:Color], you'll execute attacks
automatically. This is your standard [System:Color name=tutorial ]auto-attack[/System:Color].

Got all that? Then it's time to [System:Color name=tutorial ]draw your
weapon [/System:Color]and start preparing your lunch!

Auto-attacks are delivered in [System:Color name=tutorial ]sets of three[/System:Color].
The attack power increases with each blow.

It's also good to keep in mind that auto-attacks
have an [System:Color name=tutorial ]optimal distance[/System:Color]. Keep the perfect
distance from your enemy to maximize damage!

The icons in the [System:Color name=tutorial ]lower right[/System:Color] are called
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Arts Icons[/System:Color]. When an [System:Color name=tutorial ]Arts Icon[/System:Color] lights
up, it means an [System:Color name=tutorial ]Art[/System:Color] is ready to use.

[System:Color name=tutorial ]Arts[/System:Color] are [System:Color name=tutorial ]special techniques[/System:Color] distinct from auto-attacks.
The icons are laid out like the controller buttons,
so just press the [System:Color name=tutorial ]corresponding button[/System:Color] to use one!

After using an [System:Color name=tutorial ]Art[/System:Color], you'll have to wait until the
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Recast Gauge[/System:Color] surrounding the icon has refilled
before you can use it again.

The [System:Color name=tutorial ]Recast Gauge[/System:Color] will refill as you
auto-attack enemies.

Try pressing [System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=X ] [/System:Color]now to let rip
with Rex's[System:Color name=tutorial ] Anchor Shot[/System:Color] Art.

The enemy just dropped something!
This is an item called an [System:Color name=tutorial ]HP Potion[/System:Color].

Maneuver Rex to the [System:Color name=tutorial ]HP Potion[/System:Color] to pick it up.
It'll [System:Color name=tutorial ]restore some of his HP[/System:Color].

Some [System:Color name=tutorial ]Arts[/System:Color], like [System:Color name=tutorial ]Anchor Shot[/System:Color], will always cause the
enemy to drop an [System:Color name=tutorial ]HP Potion[/System:Color].

You can use [System:Color name=tutorial ]Arts[/System:Color] repeatedly to deal maximum damage,
or save [System:Color name=tutorial ]Arts[/System:Color] for when your HP starts getting low.
Choosing when to use your [System:Color name=tutorial ]Arts[/System:Color] is an important tactic.

See that aura effect glowing around the enemy?
This indicates that the enemy is in a [System:Color name=tutorial ]rage state[/System:Color].

Certain enemies have a tendency to become enraged
when their [System:Color name=tutorial ]HP dips below a certain level[/System:Color].

Enemies' stats will increase when enraged, so be
careful - they might be tougher than you expect!

Rex has been brought back from death's door
as the Driver of Heaven's Holy Grail.

See the gauge that just filled up?
That's the icon for your [System:Color name=tutorial ]Special[/System:Color].
Right, now let's talk [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Combos[/System:Color].
【ボタンチャレンジ】

Just now, Homura activated a [System:Color name=tutorial ]special effect[/System:Color] that
[System:Color name=tutorial ]boosts your accuracy[/System:Color]. This type of in-battle
assistance is called a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Art[/System:Color].
【必殺技①】

You should try out a Blade Combo going from a
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Fire-element [/System:Color]Special to a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Water-element [/System:Color]one.
First up, trigger Homura's [System:Color name=tutorial ]level 1[/System:Color] Special!
【ブレイドとのキズナ】
【属性コンボ②】

It's time you learned to take your teamwork to the
next level. Introducing [System:Color name=tutorial ]Chain Attacks[/System:Color], a way for your
whole party to deal massive damage to the enemy!

Homura has finally released her true power. This
tutorial explains how to use her while awakened.

You're up against a whole bunch of fierce
opponents! Here's a little tip that might
come in handy when taking on multiple enemies.

That Vandham guy is a pretty effective teacher.
Thanks to his lesson, Rex's [System:Color name=tutorial ]Anchor Shot[/System:Color] Art now
has the ability to inflict [System:Color name=tutorial ]Down[/System:Color] on foes!

Let me tell you about a special
[System:Color name=tutorial ]three-person attack[/System:Color], which only Rex can use.
【エネミーの怒り状態】
【抜刀/納刀/おびき寄せ】
【回復ポット】
【戦闘不能】
Looks like one of you has inflicted [System:Color name=tutorial ]Break[/System:Color]!
【ロール】

Well now! It seems it's finally time to talk about
[System:Color name=tutorial ]level 4 Specials[/System:Color].
【ボタンチャレンジ】

To link a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Combo[/System:Color], use a Special
[System:Color name=tutorial ]one level higher[/System:Color]. I'll raise Nia's
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Special gauge[/System:Color] to [System:Color name=tutorial ]level 2[/System:Color]. Press [System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=ZL ][/System:Color] to use it!
【ブレイドアーツ】

You may have got the gist for yourself
already, but let me go into a little
more detail on [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Combos[/System:Color].

Now that you've got three people on
your team, I'll give you a quick primer
on the [System:Color name=tutorial ]sealing effects[/System:Color] of [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Combos[/System:Color].

Before you help Nia out, let me explain a little
about how to fight when you have multiple Drivers
in your party.
【ブレイドチェンジ】
【特殊ブレイドチェンジ・ヒカリ】

Let me tell you a few things you might find
useful! First up, I'll explain the regular view.
まずは通常画面の説明をしたいと思います

See what the arrow is pointing to right now?
That's the [System:Color name=tutorial ]compass[/System:Color].

The mark on the compass indicates the direction
that Rex should be heading in.

The [System:Color name=tutorial ]digits[/System:Color] above the mark on the compass show the
[System:Color name=tutorial ]distance to your destination[/System:Color].

If Rex's destination is higher than
his current position, then you'll
see a little arrow [System:Color name=tutorial ]above [/System:Color]the marker.

Conversely, if it's at a lower altitude than Rex's
current position, then the arrow will be displayed
[System:Color name=tutorial ]below [/System:Color]the mark.

Next up, let's take a look at the [System:Color name=tutorial ]environmental
information[/System:Color] that the arrow mark is pointing to
right now.

This will key you into info about
your immediate surroundings, like
the [System:Color name=tutorial ]weather[/System:Color], [System:Color name=tutorial ]time of day[/System:Color], and so on.

You should keep in mind that Alst's environments
can change as you continue on your adventure.

These changes will never put Rex's life in
immediate danger...

But they may well affect the enemies
and townsfolk you'll run into, so it's worth
keeping an eye on the world around you!

Next, the [System:Color name=tutorial ]mini-map[/System:Color]! You can use this to get
a quick grasp of Rex's surroundings.

The yellow marker in the middle shows Rex's
current location, and the direction he's facing.

Push [System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=L3 ][/System:Color] to display the map full-screen
or hide the mini-map.

Confident adventurers might prefer to make their
way through Alst without using the mini-map.

Lastly, we have the "[System:Color name=tutorial ]Current Objective[/System:Color]".
As you might expect, this tells you exactly what
Rex is supposed to be doing at the present time.

You can toggle its visibility with [System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=ZR ][/System:Color], so take a
look if you're ever unsure about what to do next.

Right now, it's telling you to go
and pay a visit to [System:Color name=tutorial ]Meroro[/System:Color] at the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Central
Exchange[/System:Color], so try doing that!

Looks like our adventure's about to really get
going! And you can count on me to offer timely
explanations of any new game features you encounter!

When you close this tutorial screen, you'll see
"[System:Color name=tutorial ]Goldmund Return Port[/System:Color]" pop up on the screen.
This is letting you know you've found a [System:Color name=tutorial ]landmark[/System:Color].

The other types of area that you'll encounter
are [System:Color name=tutorial ]locations [/System:Color]and [System:Color name=tutorial ]Secret Areas[/System:Color].

When you've discovered a landmark, you can return
to it instantly with [System:Color name=tutorial ]Skip Travel[/System:Color], at any time.

Skip Travel is a handy feature that
lets you [System:Color name=tutorial ]travel instantly[/System:Color] to places
that you've already visited.

There's one more thing I should tell you about
Secret Areas and landmarks.

If you're defeated in battle, you'll be
returned to the last landmark that you visited.

Alst has a great variety of landmarks, so discover
as many as you can to help you on your adventure!

Time to learn about [System:Color name=tutorial ]salvaging[/System:Color]!
The icon you can see in front of Rex right now
marks what we call a "[System:Color name=tutorial ]Salvage Point[/System:Color]".

As long as you have [System:Color name=tutorial ]cylinders[/System:Color] handy,
you can go salvaging at one of these points
at any time.
When you salvage, a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Button Challenge[/System:Color] begins.

Succeeding in the Button Challenge makes
better treasure more likely, so watch
the timing and press each button well.

Worse still, you might even find yourself
hauling up a fearsome enemy, so be careful!

There are Salvage Points all over Alst, and the
type of treasure varies from point to point, so if
you find a new one, be sure to give it a try!

By the way, if you're short on cylinders,
you can buy them at any [System:Color name=tutorial ]salvager's shop[/System:Color].
You'll find these shops all across Alst.

An expensive cylinder is likely to get you better
quality treasure, but even a cheap one can yield
a decent haul. So use your gold as you see fit!

Now use the cylinder Iruiru gave you
and try salvaging right away.

Hold up a second! Before I forget, I should
probably explain how to control the [System:Color name=tutorial ]camera[/System:Color]!
The camera has two modes: [System:Color name=tutorial ]manual [/System:Color]and [System:Color name=tutorial ]auto[/System:Color].

To use [System:Color name=tutorial ]manual mode[/System:Color], just [System:Color name=tutorial ]use [ML:icon icon=R3 ][/System:Color] to point the
camera in whichever direction you like.

If you [System:Color name=tutorial ]press [ML:icon icon=R3 ][/System:Color] while the camera's
in manual mode, the camera will hone
in on Rex's back and follow him around.
This is what we call [System:Color name=tutorial ]auto mode[/System:Color].

If you experiment with different camera angles,
then you might be able to spot a few things that
you might otherwise have missed, so give it a try!

Let me quickly explain about [System:Color name=tutorial ]lodgings[/System:Color]. When you take a
[System:Color name=tutorial ]short rest[/System:Color] in a lodging facility like an inn, you can
use any [System:Color name=tutorial ]bonus EXP[/System:Color] you've earned to boost your level!

Bonus EXP is the experience that you earn when
completing quests or discovering landmarks. Be sure
to rest at inns on occasion so you can use it!

レベルの上げ方は
【すべてオート】【選択オート】【マニュアル】の
3種類があります

すべてオートを選ぶと
ボーナス経験値を使い切るまで　レベルアップします

選択オートを選ぶと　キャラクターごとにオートかマニュアルかを
選ぶことができます

While resting up, you can increase your
characters' levels as much or as little as you
like as long as you have the bonus EXP to spare.

If you run into an enemy you simply
can't defeat, try leveling up
with the Bonus EXP you've accumulated.

On the other hand, if you're the type that likes
a challenge, you're free to never level up at
lodgings at all. It can be fun to live dangerously!

あと　宿屋では【雲海の満ち引きが変わるまで休む】
という役割もあります

アルストには雲海の満ち引きによって
行ける場所　行けなくなる場所があるので
そんな時は　宿屋で一休みすると良いでしょう

Anyway, you've got a big day ahead of you
tomorrow. You'd better get some shut-eye!

What you're looking at right now is a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Collection
Point[/System:Color]. Check here to uncover [System:Color name=tutorial ]collectible items[/System:Color].

You'll find Collection Points all
over Alst, and each area will have
its own selection of items to discover.

Also, there are some Collection Points where
you can use Blades' [System:Color name=tutorial ]Field Skills[/System:Color] to find special
collectible items that you couldn't get otherwise.

The collectibles that you find are sure to come in
handy during your adventure, so if you come across
a Collection Point, be sure to check it out!

Looks like something's blocking your way up ahead.
But if your Blades have the right [System:Color name=tutorial ]Field Skills[/System:Color],
then you might be able overcome obstacles like this!
Try investigating that [System:Color name=tutorial ]fallen tree[/System:Color].

As you can see, you used Homura's [System:Color name=tutorial ]Fire Mastery[/System:Color] to
burn it up and get it out of your way.

If you want to see all the Field Skills
Homura can use, go to [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu [/System:Color]>
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Setup [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Info[/System:Color].

There's a lot of places in Alst that
you won't be able to get to if you
don't have the right Field Skills.

Even if an obstacle seems impassable at first,
it's worth getting a bit closer to see if you can
do something about it.

Anyway, let's keep moving and see if we can
find Nia anywhere!

You can now use the Skip Time feature to
skip instantly to whatever time of day you prefer.
That's pretty handy!

Both people and enemies may behave differently
depending on the time of day.

Try different things and see what new discoveries
you can make.

A number of shops are now available for you
to use! You'll find a whole range of different
traders as you journey across Alst.

[System:Color name=tutorial ]Trading shops[/System:Color] barter for treasures,
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Information Shops[/System:Color] sell information, and
[System:Color name=tutorial ]lifestyle shops[/System:Color] sell your favorite items.

You'll also come across [System:Color name=tutorial ]salvager's shops[/System:Color]
for stocking up on cylinders, or [System:Color name=tutorial ]accessory
shops[/System:Color] where you can buy useful items to wear.

You may have already come across some of these,
of course. From now on, feel free to make use
of any of the categories of shop I just mentioned!

Avaritia Trading Company is known as the hub
of Alst's commerce, so naturally, you'll
find a plethora of different shops here.

While you're here, you should make sure you've got
everything you need before you head out on your
adventures!

Oh! I almost forgot to tell you about something
important...Rex's [System:Color name=tutorial ]pouch[/System:Color]!

Rex never goes anywhere without his handy pouch.
It's great for putting his [System:Color name=tutorial ]favorite items [/System:Color]inside
so that he always has them close to hand.

Rex's pouch isn't that big - it can hold just
one handy item at a time.

Lifestyle shops sell Pouch Items.
The items you keep in your pouch grant
various effects during your adventure.

There are 12 different types of lifestyle shops
across Alst, so if you encounter a new one,
be sure to check it out!

You finally got that [System:Color name=tutorial ]Abyss Vest [/System:Color]you always wanted!
It'll boost your maximum HP by 24%.

Right now, the Abyss Vest is the only accessory
you have, but you're sure to encounter
a whole lot more during your adventure!

Equip accessories to gain their effects.
Open [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters[/System:Color] >
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Character Setup[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Equip Accessories[/System:Color].

You accepted a [System:Color name=tutorial ]quest[/System:Color]! There are two
types of quest: [System:Color name=tutorial ]regular quests[/System:Color], and ones
that are part of the [System:Color name=tutorial ]main story[/System:Color].

You'll need to complete main story quests to advance
the main story. The direction of the next location is
shown on the compass as a [System:Color name=tutorial ]pink exclamation mark icon[/System:Color].

Many people in Alst need help.
Look for a [System:Color name=tutorial ]blue question mark icon[/System:Color] above
their heads.

If you speak to them, they'll usually open up to you
about their problems and request some kind of help.
These are the regular quests that I mentioned earlier!

I'm sure if you manage to solve
their problems, they'll give you
some kind of reward for your trouble!

Ordinary quests aren't vital for the main
story. Follow the [System:Color name=tutorial ]blue exclamation mark
icon [/System:Color]to get to the next destination.

Now here's an important point to keep in mind:
The destination marker on the compass will only
be shown for the currently [System:Color name=tutorial ]active [/System:Color]quest.

You can change which quest is active
from your [System:Color name=tutorial ]Quest Log[/System:Color] in the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu[/System:Color].

But remember: you can only have one
quest set to active at any given time.

There's no limit to the quests you can accept.
Talk to anyone you see with a blue
question mark icon above their head!

You've just acquired new comrades to accompany you
on your adventure! You can adjust the setup of your
party in [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Formation Change[/System:Color].

No matter how many friends you make, you will
never be able to take more than [System:Color name=tutorial ]three party
members [/System:Color]into battle at once, so choose carefully!

The character set to [System:Color name=tutorial ]No. 1 [/System:Color]in Formation
Change will be the [System:Color name=tutorial ]character that you control[/System:Color].

No two characters fight in exactly the same way,
so you should experiment with a few and find
who fits your play style the best.

I'm sure you're itching to get searching for
Gramps and Nia, but I should warn you that you'll
probably encounter a few enemies on the way!

You'll want to be prepared for that, so I'd better
quickly fill you in on how Rex gets stronger and
improves his capabilities.

Among the things you'll earn
for completing a battle are two
important types of points: [System:Color name=tutorial ]WP [/System:Color]and [System:Color name=tutorial ]SP[/System:Color].

WP stands for [System:Color name=tutorial ]Weapon Points[/System:Color]. You can think of these
as a measure of the [System:Color name=tutorial ]level of skill [/System:Color]that Rex has with
his [System:Color name=tutorial ]weapon[/System:Color], and you'll need them to [System:Color name=tutorial ]level up Arts[/System:Color].

The same Art will deal much higher damage
to enemies at higher levels, so it's worth
strengthening your Arts at the earliest opportunity!

Give it a go by heading to [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu [/System:Color]>
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Character Setup [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Enhance Arts[/System:Color].

One thing to keep in mind is that Arts enhancement
has level requirements.

If Rex himself hasn't reached a high
enough level, he won't be able
to enhance his Arts beyond that point.

By the way, the Enhance Arts menu also allows you
to select which Art is assigned to which button.

SP, meanwhile, stands for [System:Color name=tutorial ]Skill Points[/System:Color]. These
represent how well Rex is [System:Color name=tutorial ]trained in his battle
techniques[/System:Color], and they're used to unlock passive [System:Color name=tutorial ]skills[/System:Color].

Try giving Rex some new skills in [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu [/System:Color]>
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Character Setup[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Bonding Ring[/System:Color].

Rex's ability to [System:Color name=tutorial ]resonate with Core
Crystals [/System:Color]has been unlocked!

You can resonate with a new Blade at any time by
going to [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blades[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Resonance[/System:Color].

There are three ranks of Core
Crystal: [System:Color name=tutorial ]Common[/System:Color], [System:Color name=tutorial ]Rare[/System:Color], and [System:Color name=tutorial ]Epic[/System:Color].

The higher the Core Crystal's rank,
the greater the chance that resonance will
produce a Blade with an unusual appearance.

Core Crystals aren't much use just lying around,
so it can't hurt to resonate with them and see
what you get!

Once you have yourself a new Blade,
you'll need to [System:Color name=tutorial ]engage it [/System:Color]so that it can
take part in battle.

Add Blades to your battle party in [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu [/System:Color]>
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Character Setup [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Engage[/System:Color].

Up until now, Rex has had to rely on Homura alone
for support in battle...

...but now you'll be able to engage a variety of
other Blades and expand your support options!

To take advantage of different Blades in battle,
press the directional button corresponding to each
Blade's face icon and perform a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Switch[/System:Color].

A Blade Switch changes which
Blade supports you during battle.

Of course, switching Blades will change both your
[System:Color name=tutorial ]weapon[/System:Color] and your [System:Color name=tutorial ]available Arts[/System:Color].

Different weapons have different benefits
and drawbacks in battle, so use Blade Switches
tactically after considering the current situation.

A word of warning: once you've performed a Blade
Switch, it'll be a little while before your
previous Blade will be available for use again.

However, Rex can build [System:Color name=tutorial ]Trust [/System:Color]with his Blades.
The higher your Trust, the less time you'll have
to wait to call for support from that Blade again!

[System:Color name=tutorial ]Getting a Blade's Bonding Gifts will increase
Trust[/System:Color], so when you get a new Blade, remember
to try and complete as many as possible!

Behold Hana, Alst's first artificial Blade! Since Hana
is man-made (or should that be...Nopon-made?), she
can't make use of [System:Color name=tutorial ]Assist Cores[/System:Color] like a regular Blade.

Behold Hana, the world's first Artificial Blade! Hana
can't equip Assist Cores, but she has something just
as good for customizing her abilities: [System:Color name=tutorial ]Hana Rise[/System:Color]!

You can access Hana Rise by going to [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu[/System:Color] >
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Setup[/System:Color] ([System:Color name=tutorial ]Hana JS[/System:Color]) > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Hana Rise[/System:Color].

To make use of the Hana Rise feature,
you'll need to get hold of certain
items via the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Tiger! Tiger![/System:Color] game.

Play Tiger! Tiger! as much as you can to make
Hana into her best self!

Looks like you've got Nia back safe and sound!
Now you've got three members in your party,
I should explain about [System:Color name=tutorial ]roles[/System:Color] and [System:Color name=tutorial ]classes[/System:Color].

Blades are born with three roles: [System:Color name=tutorial ]Attack[/System:Color] ([System:Color name=tutorial ]ATK[/System:Color]),
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Recovery[/System:Color] ([System:Color name=tutorial ]REC[/System:Color]), and [System:Color name=tutorial ]Defense[/System:Color] ([System:Color name=tutorial ]DEF[/System:Color]). For example,
Homura's role is Attack, and Byakko's is Recovery.

The types of Blade that a Driver engages will determine
their fighting style. Each Driver's fighting style
will fall into certain categories, called [System:Color name=tutorial ]Classes[/System:Color].

Some Classes emphasize attack, some defense,
or some strike a balance between Roles,
and each Class has its own [System:Color name=tutorial ]special effects[/System:Color].

Engage your favorite Blades or pick them
strategically for a strong Class.
Experiment to suit your play style!

Generally, Blades can't change Roles. As
an Artificial Blade, [System:Color name=tutorial ]Hana[/System:Color] is the exception. She
can [System:Color name=tutorial ]change her Role[/System:Color] using her [System:Color name=tutorial ]Hana Rise[/System:Color] feature.

Play [System:Color name=tutorial ]Tiger! Tiger![/System:Color] to obtain different [System:Color name=tutorial ]Role CPU[/System:Color]s
and use them to change Hana's Role in Hana Rise.

Now if you've got all that, let's get back to
the game and make our escape!

It's time to let you in on a handy
battle tactic... How to [System:Color name=tutorial ]lure [/System:Color]enemies!

If you target an enemy from a distance [System:Color name=tutorial ]without
drawing your weapon[/System:Color] and [System:Color name=tutorial ]press [ML:icon icon=down ][/System:Color], you can lure
an enemy toward you.

It's useful for taking out a herd of enemies one
by one, or for when you'd prefer to fight an
opponent in a wider space.

Try luring over that enemy in front
of you now! First, target it with [System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=R ][/System:Color],
then press [System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=down ] [/System:Color]to lure it over!

You've arrived in [System:Color name=tutorial ]Torigo[/System:Color], Gula's largest
settlement! So now's a good time to talk about
[System:Color name=tutorial ]developing towns[/System:Color].

Avaritia, Gormott, and other towns
across Alst have [System:Color name=tutorial ]five Development Levels[/System:Color].

A town's Development Level can
be raised by earning [System:Color name=tutorial ]Dev Points[/System:Color].

When a town's Dev Level goes up, then you can
expect the [System:Color name=tutorial ]price of goods in shops to go down[/System:Color]!

Some shops might even expand their ranges and sell
never-before-seen products.

You can [System:Color name=tutorial ]earn Dev Points [/System:Color]by [System:Color name=tutorial ]completing quests [/System:Color]and
resolving residents' difficulties.

It's also possible to [System:Color name=tutorial ]earn a few Dev
Points [/System:Color]just by [System:Color name=tutorial ]talking to people you meet[/System:Color].

You can view the Dev Level of a town any
time you go shopping, and also by going
to [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Skip Travel[/System:Color].

As a public-spirited citizen of Alst,
you should do all you can to raise
the Dev Level of its settlements!

Alst is a world surrounded by the Cloud Sea. As
Rex and his friends said, the Cloud Sea has [System:Color name=tutorial ]tides[/System:Color].

The shifting tides will close off places that you could
once visit, as well as opening up places that you 
couldn't reach, so plan your adventure accordingly!

Hold on! I almost forgot to tell you about
something really important - how to [System:Color name=tutorial ]develop
your Blade's capabilities[/System:Color]!

There are three main ways to develop a Blade:
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Weapon Enhancement[/System:Color], [System:Color name=tutorial ]equipping Assist Cores[/System:Color], and
the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Bonding Ring[/System:Color].

Weapon Enhancement strengthens a Blade's
inborn weapon using Core Chips.

You can apply Core Chips to weapons in [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu[/System:Color] >
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Setup[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Weapon Enhancement[/System:Color].

If you come across a shop selling Core Chips
during your adventure, it's always a good idea to
invest in some new ones!

It's said some Core Chips not only
raise a weapon's basic performance,
but also activate special abilities.

You might even come across enemies carrying
special Core Chips during your travels.

However you obtain them, you can apply Core Chips
to weapons by going to [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters [/System:Color]>
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Setup [/System:Color]> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Weapon Enhancement[/System:Color].

Next, let's talk about the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Bonding Ring[/System:Color].
This is a chart which shows the range
of proficiencies available to a specific Blade.

Here you can acquire [System:Color name=tutorial ]Field Skills[/System:Color]
for overcoming field obstacles and strengthen
the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Specials[/System:Color] you use in battle.

These abilities and power-ups can be had by fulfilling
the conditions for the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Bonding Gifts[/System:Color] on the Bonding
Ring. There's a whole host of goals for you to aim for.

Finally, we have [System:Color name=tutorial ]Assist Cores[/System:Color]. These are like
accessories specifically for Blades to equip.

You'll be sure to happen across Assist Cores from
time to time as you continue with your journey.

However, you won't be able to equip
Assist Cores that you find right away.

At an [System:Color name=tutorial ]Assist Core Shop[/System:Color] in town, you need to [System:Color name=tutorial ]Build[/System:Color]
([System:Color name=tutorial ]refine[/System:Color]) Assist Cores. Ask there for the details.

Before your big job begins, there's one more
kind of shop to explain: the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Trading Shop[/System:Color].

You may have already made use of them,
but there are businesses called item trading shops
that specialize in taking [System:Color name=tutorial ]treasure[/System:Color] off your hands.

If you sell off items as a whole set,
you'll earn a bunch more money than
if you sold them off individually.

Well, item trading shops are a bit different.
They differ from normal shops in two ways: they
only buy in [System:Color name=tutorial ]bulk[/System:Color], and they [System:Color name=tutorial ]specialise in treasure[/System:Color].

For example, if you take some treasure you've
salvaged to a regular shop, then they might only
pay you 20G for it.

But if you took the same items to a trading shop,
they might buy a set of three from you for 100G.

The key thing to keep in mind with item traders is that
they're very selective about the wares they accept.
They'll only buy your items in predefined sets.

A successful trade raises the sale price,
and you may receive items as well!

So when you find precious treasures, don't just sell
them off cheap at a regular shop. See if you can put
together sets for trading shops and make a tidy profit!

You're standing in front of an [System:Color name=tutorial ]Assist
Core Shop[/System:Color], so let's review. Here you
can [System:Color name=tutorial ]build unrefined Assist Cores[/System:Color].

To build an Assist Core, you'll need
[System:Color name=tutorial ]collectible items[/System:Color].

The number of collectible items you'll need is
defined individually for each Assist Core.

Once you have the required number of collectible
items, you can build the Assist Core at the shop.

But watch out! The higher the value of the
Assist Core, the more difficult it's likely to be
to find all of the necessary items.

If you want to build unrefined Assist
Cores quickly, make a habit of gathering
collectible items at Collection Points.

Ah, it looks like you've found a treasure
trove! But as you may have noticed, it's
a little different from the regular kind.

The icon above the box indicates that you'll need
the help of your Blades' [System:Color name=tutorial ]Field Skills [/System:Color]to open it.

But even if you can't open a treasure trove
right away, there's no need to despair!

If you develop your Blades and help them to acquire
Field Skills from the Bonding Ring, someday you'll
surely be able to open it up and see what's inside.

You now have the option to take [System:Color name=tutorial ]long rests[/System:Color] at
[System:Color name=tutorial ]lodging facilities[/System:Color]. This lets you rest until the
[System:Color name=tutorial ]tides of the Cloud Sea[/System:Color] have shifted.

If you ever find that your way is blocked due to the
shifting tides of the Cloud Sea, then just go back
and have a long rest, whether you're tired or not.

Since the tides of the Cloud Sea change every time
you have a long rest, it's wise to check the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Cloud Sea
status[/System:Color] in the [System:Color name=tutorial ]environmental information[/System:Color] display first.

Oh, and you should bear in mind that it's not
possible to take a long rest at every single
lodging facility in Alst.

But you certainly can in the one in Torigo, which
is just as well, because Torigo is quite sensitive
to the comings and goings of the Cloud Sea!

Looks like you've become the leader of the
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Hræsvelgr Mercenaries[/System:Color]. Congratulations! Let's
take a moment to go over what Yuu just told us.

Mercs can expect to field requests
for all kinds of [System:Color name=tutorial ]missions[/System:Color].

Usually, you'll get a notification on the right
of the screen when a new Merc Mission becomes
available, but you can also check them in the menu.

Additionally, if you run into someone who looks
like they're having some kind of problem, you might
be able to accept a mission from them directly.

Just bear in mind that there are two types of Merc
Mission: missions that can [System:Color name=tutorial ]only be done once[/System:Color], and
missions you can do [System:Color name=tutorial ]over and over again[/System:Color].

The next point is about the importance of making sure
that you [System:Color name=tutorial ]build the right team for the job[/System:Color]. For each
mission, you'll need to put together a squad of Blades.

If you look carefully at the job details,
you should be able to figure out [System:Color name=tutorial ]which skills
you'll need the Blades you send to have[/System:Color].

If you send a squad with the right skills,
then you'll greatly reduce the amount
of time it takes to complete the mission.

Blades can [System:Color name=tutorial ]get achievements
in the Bonding Ring[/System:Color] if they're part
of squad that [System:Color name=tutorial ]fulfills a Merc Mission[/System:Color].

So, even while they aren't accompanying you on
your adventure, if you keep them busy with Merc
Missions, they can come back stronger than ever!

By the way, your mercenary band has
a [System:Color name=tutorial ]level[/System:Color] of its own, which can be
raised by completing certain missions.

When you think the band might be ready to
size up to the next level, go and talk to Yuu -
I'm sure he'll point you in the right direction.

As the Merc Group Level rises, you can take on
more difficult missions.

As settlements develop, special missions
may become available. Completing them
may change the goods sold in shops.

So, to summarize: [System:Color name=tutorial ]accept a mission[/System:Color], then
[System:Color name=tutorial ]form a squad of Blades[/System:Color].

Then you [System:Color name=tutorial ]fulfill the mission[/System:Color].
And finally, you [System:Color name=tutorial ]reap the rewards[/System:Color]!

Best of luck! I'm sure you'll
be a great Merc leader!

See that icon floating over there?
It indicates the location of a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Bonding Talk[/System:Color].

Bonding Talks are important events that deepen
the bonds between your companions.

You'll run into these icons all over Alst,
so it's a good idea to check them out as you
encounter them!

Viewing Bonding Talk is sure to give a
[System:Color name=tutorial ]big boost[/System:Color] to the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Trust Level[/System:Color] between your
Drivers and Blades!

Think carefully before answering any options that are
presented to you during the Bonding Talk, as your
responses will affect the amount of Trust gained.

To view a Bonding Talk, you'll need to have the right
people present in your party, at the right time of day.
You can view the conditions by accessing the icon.

Sometimes you'll find the icon does nothing
unless you access it with the right party members
or at the right time of day.

It's also worth keeping in mind that viewing some
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Bonding Talk [/System:Color]counts as an [System:Color name=tutorial ]achievement [/System:Color]on a
Blade's Bonding Ring.

Bonding Talks are essential if you want
to develop your Blades.

One more thing... You can often find
out the location of Bonding Talk after
resting at lodgings such as inns.

Viewing Bonding Talk greatly increases Trust with
your Blade. Experience lots of them to deepen
your bond even further!

So you might need a quick primer on
how a Driver fights!

First, let's explain [System:Color name=tutorial ]Bonding[/System:Color].
See the [System:Color name=tutorial ]band of light [/System:Color]connecting Rex and Homura?
That's Bonding.

When a Driver and Blade's hearts
are truly in sync, this bond will
start to glow with a [System:Color name=tutorial ]golden light[/System:Color].

When Bonding glows golden, it's a sign that the minds
of Blade and Driver are in harmony. [System:Color name=tutorial ]Movement speed[/System:Color]
will go up, and [System:Color name=tutorial ]Arts Recast speed[/System:Color] will speed up.

It'll even provide some serious boosts to his
basic attack power.

You can strengthen Bonding in battle by staying
physically close to your Blade and hitting
home with as many attacks as possible.

But other factors can also have an effect,
such as battling skillfully by dealing a lot of
attacks in succession.

On the other hand, if there's too much distance,
Bonding weakens, which also weakens the Driver. Keep
your Bonding with Homura in mind when fighting Metsu!

Rex is in trouble if this happens - his
fighting strength will start to dissipate.

Fight Metsu while keeping your
Bonding with Homura in mind!

[System:Color name=tutorial ]Specials [/System:Color]are among the most powerful attacks in
a Driver's arsenal, far outclassing ordinary Arts.

Even after your Special is ready,
you can [System:Color name=tutorial ]keep charging its gauge[/System:Color]
to increase its level and power.
Specials are [System:Color name=tutorial ]charged up[/System:Color] by attacking with Arts.
You can charge Specials to [System:Color name=tutorial ]three levels of power[/System:Color].

If you [System:Color name=tutorial ]use an Art as an auto-attack hits,
you'll fill the gauge more[/System:Color].
A circular sign indicates success.

Also, when you use a Special, you'll need to
execute a [System:Color name=tutorial ]button challenge[/System:Color].

Follow the prompts and [System:Color name=tutorial ]press the buttons at the
right time[/System:Color]. Succeed, and the damage will double.

Attacking the enemy with a Special may even
give you a chance to perform a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Combo[/System:Color]...but
I'll tell you more about that another time.

After you assault an enemy with a Special, you'll see
a [System:Color name=tutorial ]gauge [/System:Color]at the top of the screen indicating the [System:Color name=tutorial ]window
of opportunity[/System:Color] in which you can use a Blade Combo.

The [System:Color name=tutorial ]possible Routes [/System:Color]for the Blade Combo
will also be displayed on screen.

If you can hit the enemy with another, higher-staged
Special before the gauge [System:Color name=tutorial ]runs out[/System:Color], you'll deal [System:Color name=tutorial ]much
more damage [/System:Color]than a regular Special.

The enemy's just been hit with a Special. I'll
bump up your Special level for you just this
once, so try to catch them with a Blade Combo!

[System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Arts [/System:Color]are one of the tools in a Blade's
arsenal, and Blades will use them [System:Color name=tutorial ]automatically
during battle to support their Driver[/System:Color].

The higher your Trust with a Blade,
the more likely that Blade is to support you.

As for Trust...that's a topic for later.
We can go into the details when you've gained
a bit more experience as a Driver.

Right now, you should probably
focus on defeating Metsu.

Now we've got ourselves a decent sized party,
it's worth knowing how to deal with [System:Color name=tutorial ]aggro[/System:Color].

I daresay you've already noticed, but while a
Driver is being attacked by an enemy, they'll
be marked with a [System:Color name=tutorial ]red ring[/System:Color].

We call this the "[System:Color name=tutorial ]Aggro Ring[/System:Color]".
The [System:Color name=tutorial ]wedges[/System:Color] on the ring show
[System:Color name=tutorial ]the direction of the enemy attacking you[/System:Color].

Aggro is a measure of an enemy's aggression toward the
Drivers they're fighting. The more viciously you attack
an enemy, the more it'll want to attack you back.

If a Healer-class Driver draws aggro,
they're much more likely to be incapacitated.
Right now, Nia should avoid drawing aggro.

Drivers that have defense-orientated Classes are better
equipped to draw aggro and absorb enemy attacks. So,
right now, it's better for Tora to have the most aggro.

Drivers with Fighter-type Classes are the ones
that focus on dealing damage to the enemy. That's
Rex, so make him the mainstay of your offense!

Guards draw enemy aggro, Healers
restore Guards' HP, and Fighters
reduce the enemy's HP.

Take a look at the indicators the arrow is pointing
to. These show the various [System:Color name=tutorial ]sealing effects[/System:Color] that can
be applied if you execute a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Stage 3 Blade Combo[/System:Color].

The final Special you use in the Blade Combo
will determine which sealing effect is inflicted,
depending on the combo route.

Once inflicted, a sealing effect will continue
until it gets [System:Color name=tutorial ]overwritten by another seal[/System:Color].

Regardless of type, sealing your enemy puts you
at a massive advantage, so you should go all out
to try and hit home with a Stage 3 Blade Combo!

However, there is one drawback to be aware of: when
you hit an enemy with a Stage 3 Blade Combo, they'll
acquire a [System:Color name=tutorial ]resistance[/System:Color] to that Combo's element.

This means that using the same combo route
repeatedly will deal much less damage.

So when you use Blade Combos, you
should experiment with different routes!

The world of Alst still contains many zoological
enigmas, just waiting to be solved.

If you try targeting all sorts of enemies, you'll
occasionally encounter ones whose [System:Color name=tutorial ]target icon
looks different from that of normal enemies[/System:Color].

We call those [System:Color name=tutorial ]unique monsters[/System:Color], and they're
a little bit special.

Unique monsters are much tougher than the
regular kind. Even the strongest Drivers in Alst
often have trouble with them.

So if you take down a unique monster, you'll
surely earn the respect of people all over Alst!

Unlike ordinary monsters, they unleash
powerful attacks. Prepare well
before challenging them.

If you defeat a unique monster,
a tombstone will remain at the site where
it fell, in memory of its legendary life.

Some even say that if you press [ML:icon icon=A ] at the
tombstone, the monster will rise from its grave
to reclaim its former glory!

Rex is a Driver of Heaven's Holy Grail! The power
of the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Master Driver[/System:Color] has awoken within him!

Nia has revealed her true form.
Rex can now [System:Color name=tutorial ]engage Nia as a Blade[/System:Color].

You can now summon Hikari or Homura depending on
Rex's requirements.

The icon that the arrow is pointing to right now
indicates the enemy's [System:Color name=tutorial ]weakness[/System:Color].

Since it's a [System:Color name=tutorial ]fire icon[/System:Color], this enemy
is [System:Color name=tutorial ]weak against fire[/System:Color]. So Homura's
got something of an advantage here!

Next, let's talk about how to get party
members [System:Color name=tutorial ]back on their feet[/System:Color]. When a Driver's
HP hits zero, they'll be incapacitated.

When the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Party Gauge[/System:Color] shown by the arrow has
charge, approach an incapacitated ally and press
[ML:icon icon=A ] to spend one segment and revive them.

Even if you're incapacitated yourself, your party
members can come and revive you in the same way.
You just need enough charge in the Party Gauge!

I also need to tell you about [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Combos[/System:Color]... But to
do that, first we'll need to launch a Special. I'll
fill up your Special Gauge this time, so fire away!

However, simply using Anchor Shot
won't necessarily inflict Down on the enemy.

Wait until the enemy is in [System:Color name=tutorial ]Break[/System:Color],
then use Anchor Shot to inflict Down.

[System:Color name=tutorial ]Nia[/System:Color] has an Art that can inflict [System:Color name=tutorial ]Break[/System:Color] on
the enemy, so for maximum effect, wait for her
to set you up before unleashing Anchor Shot!

See the gauge the arrow is pointing at?
This is the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Driver Combo gauge[/System:Color], and it will appear
whenever someone inflicts [System:Color name=tutorial ]Break[/System:Color] on the enemy.

Use an Art that has a Down effect before that gauge
runs out, and you'll have the opportunity to inflict
major damage. This is what we call a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Driver Combo[/System:Color].

A Driver Combo can be extended through
up to four stages in total:
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Break[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Down[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Rising[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Smash[/System:Color].

You'll find Rex and his friends have a variety of
Arts that can be integrated into a Driver Combo, so
try to find the best ways to link them all together!

Before that, use [System:Color name=tutorial ]Anchor Shot[/System:Color] to inflict
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Down[/System:Color] on the Ardun after Nia inflicts [System:Color name=tutorial ]Break[/System:Color].

Perhaps you've made use of it already,
but that thing that the arrow is currently
pointing to is called the [System:Color name=tutorial ]concentration icon[/System:Color].

When you're taking on multiple enemies, even if you
switch the leader's target, your allies won't switch
theirs. They'll carry on attacking the same enemies.

If you feel like you need some help, just press
[System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=left ][/System:Color], the button for the concentration icon, and your
allies will all hone in on the same enemy as you.

In a crowded battle, the order you choose to
take down enemies in can mean the difference
between victory and utter failure.

Make good use of [System:Color name=tutorial ]target-switching[/System:Color] and have your allies
[System:Color name=tutorial ]concentrate[/System:Color] on enemies, and you might find a way
out of some sticky situations. Now, protect Homura!

This means that Rex can [System:Color name=tutorial ]freely engage[/System:Color] Blades that
originally resonated with other Drivers.

You're engaged with Kagutsuchi now.
Draw out her full power and show
that you can match Meleph!

Naturally, Nia can still maintain
her [System:Color name=tutorial ]Driver form[/System:Color] while traveling.

When you want to engage Nia as a Blade, go to
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters[/System:Color], [System:Color name=tutorial ]then select the Driver Nia
and press [ML:icon icon=Y ][/System:Color].

When you want to travel with Nia in her Driver
form, go to [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters[/System:Color],
[System:Color name=tutorial ]then select the Blade Nia and press [ML:icon icon=Y ][/System:Color].

To switch them outside of battle, go to [System:Color name=tutorial ]Main Menu[/System:Color]
> [System:Color name=tutorial ]Characters[/System:Color] > [System:Color name=tutorial ]Homura[/System:Color] ([System:Color name=tutorial ]Hikari[/System:Color]) and [System:Color name=tutorial ]press [ML:icon icon=Y ][/System:Color].

During battle, you can switch between
them by pressing the button assigned
to [System:Color name=tutorial ]Homura and Hikari's Blade Switch icon[/System:Color].

Unlike with a regular [System:Color name=tutorial ]Blade Switch[/System:Color], there's
no cooldown timer for changing between Homura
and Hikari, so feel free to switch it up whenever!

The indicator the arrow is pointing at right now
represents a [System:Color name=tutorial ]combo request[/System:Color] from a Blade currently
engaged by the [System:Color name=tutorial ]character you're controlling[/System:Color].

This is displayed when one of your currently
engaged Blades' Specials would be able to
[System:Color name=tutorial ]initiate a Blade Combo[/System:Color]...

...and also when one of those Blades' Specials
would be able to [System:Color name=tutorial ]extend a Blade Combo that's
currently in progress[/System:Color].

Blade Combos can have a massive
impact on the battlefield, so try
not to miss these opportunities!

First, let's take a look at the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Party Gauge[/System:Color]. We may
have touched on this before, but it has more uses
than just getting your allies back on their feet!

When all three sections of the Party Gauge
are fully charged, you're ready to launch a
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Chain Attack [/System:Color]by pressing [System:Color name=tutorial ][ML:icon icon=plus ][/System:Color].

During a Chain Attack, each of your party members
in turn can choose one of their [System:Color name=tutorial ]currently engaged
Blades[/System:Color] to perform a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Special[/System:Color] with.

For example, first Rex might choose to use
a Special with Homura, then Nia might choose
Byakko, and finally Tora can use one with Hana.
Once everyone's had a turn, that's a single [System:Color name=tutorial ]round[/System:Color].

During a Chain Attack, choosing
a Blade's Special lets you [System:Color name=tutorial ]destroy[/System:Color]
[System:Color name=tutorial ]element orbs[/System:Color] attached to the enemy.

If you use a [System:Color name=tutorial ]Special with an opposing element[/System:Color]
against an element orb, it'll be easier to smash,
and you'll do [System:Color name=tutorial ]massive damage[/System:Color] if it does smash.

So think carefully about the order in which you
summon your Blades, and which Specials you use.

Attacking with Blades that [System:Color name=tutorial ]don't have the
opposing element[/System:Color], meanwhile, will deal just
[System:Color name=tutorial ]one point of damage[/System:Color] to a [System:Color name=tutorial ]random orb[/System:Color].

Performing a Special will incur cooldown for that
Blade, but if you manage to [System:Color name=tutorial ]burst[/System:Color] an [System:Color name=tutorial ]element orb[/System:Color],
you'll [System:Color name=tutorial ]recover half of their cooldown[/System:Color].

Bursting an element orb during a round lets you
[System:Color name=tutorial ]extend the Chain Attack by another round[/System:Color].

Bursting a lot of element orbs can have a [System:Color name=tutorial ]massive
impact[/System:Color] on the [System:Color name=tutorial ]damage multiplier[/System:Color] applied at the
end of the Chain Attack.

When the round is extended, you'll have to execute
a [System:Color name=tutorial ]button challenge[/System:Color]. If you [System:Color name=tutorial ]succeed[/System:Color], this will also
recover some of the Blades' [System:Color name=tutorial ]cooldown[/System:Color].

This button challenge is important for another
reason. Usually, when selecting a Blade to perform
a Special, their [System:Color name=tutorial ]Lv 1 Special[/System:Color] will be used...

...but [System:Color name=tutorial ]succeeding[/System:Color] in button challenges will [System:Color name=tutorial ]raise
the level[/System:Color] of the Special to a [System:Color name=tutorial ]maximum of three[/System:Color].

However, be careful, because if you
[System:Color name=tutorial ]fail[/System:Color] a button challenge, then the [System:Color name=tutorial ]level[/System:Color]
of the Special will [System:Color name=tutorial ]go down by one level[/System:Color].

Finally, it's worth remembering that launching a
Chain Attack will [System:Color name=tutorial ]use up your entire Party Gauge[/System:Color],
so be sure to save it for the right moment.

While the Chain Attack is active, though, enemies
won't attack at all. This gives you a bit of time
to figure out how best to burst those element orbs!

If you get all the way to [System:Color name=tutorial ]max Bonding[/System:Color], the [System:Color name=tutorial ]Trust
level [/System:Color]between Blade and Driver will increase.

Increasing Trust has plenty
of advantages of its own, but that
explanation can wait for another time.

We're off to Torigo now!
As your adventure continues, your Blades'
[System:Color name=tutorial ]Trust[/System:Color] will become increasingly important.

Trust is a vital resource that you need to [System:Color name=tutorial ]unlock
levels[/System:Color] on your Blade's [System:Color name=tutorial ]Bonding Ring[/System:Color].

So if you want to maximize the support
